item.content:encoded:
On September 24th and 25th, The Lagos Bridal Show brought together designers, beauty brands, hospitality partners, media, industry professionals and couples for a two-day celebration of Nigerian bridal fashion, creativity and the business of weddings.

Held at Federal Palace Hotel & Casino, Lagos, the inaugural edition of The Lagos Bridal Show was created to fill a significant gap in Nigeria’s fashion and wedding landscape: a dedicated platform where bridal designers and brands could showcase their work, connect directly with their target audience, and position Nigerian bridal fashion on a more global stage.

And it delivered exactly that.

Two Days, One Celebration of Bridal Fashion

The experience began on September 24th with an intimate media parley, bringing together members of the press, designers, sponsors, and key voices within Nigeria’s bridal industry. The press briefing featured Blessing Osih of Ekulo Group, Ese Alagbogu of Lush Hair, and May Yul-Edochie of QM Beauty Cosmetics, hosted by the founder, Rhoda Ebun, creative director of RTF Company.

The day featured a press briefing, a Meet the Designers soirée, conversations with sponsors and an engaging panel discussion titled “The Future of Nigeria’s Bridal Industry: Creativity, Innovation and Global Opportunities.”

The conversation brought together industry voices including Kola Kuddus, President of the Fashion Designers Association of Nigeria; designer Shadiat Kosoko; Fashion Editor Fade Awolesi; and fashion stylist and creative director Dipo Ayo-Adeusi. The Panel Session was hosted by Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi.

Beyond the runway, the discussion reinforced an important message: Nigerian bridal fashion has the creativity, craftsmanship and cultural relevance to compete globally, but the industry needs stronger platforms, infrastructure and opportunities to connect its talent with the right audiences.

Day two transformed Federal Palace Hotel & Casino into a glamorous bridal fashion destination.

Guests arrived for the Black Carpet, cocktails and brand activations before taking their seats for the main runway show, which brought together an exciting mix of established and emerging Nigerian fashion talent.

The runway featured TitiBelo X Hattabelles, Yemi Shoyemi, David Wej, HennyGee, Esperanza, LUSH Hair, Zayoma, Telvin Nwafor, Botu X Christine Atelier and Bibi Lawrence, each bringing a distinct interpretation of what modern Nigerian bridal style can look like.

From contemporary silhouettes and traditional influences to statement detailing and elevated occasion wear, the collections demonstrated the breadth of Nigeria’s bridal fashion landscape.

Beauty Was Just as Important as the Dress

At The Lagos Bridal Show, the complete bridal look extended beyond the clothes.

As Lead Sponsor, LUSH Hair played a major role in creating the runway beauty experience, taking responsibility for the hair styling of the models. The brand helped translate the designers’ creative direction into polished runway looks, proving that hair is an essential part of the overall bridal fashion story.

The collaboration was particularly fitting for a show centred around the modern Nigerian bride, whose wedding-day beauty is increasingly about individuality, versatility and making a statement.

Completing the beauty looks was QM Beauty Cosmetics, which handled makeup for the models throughout the runway show. Their work helped create cohesive beauty looks that complemented the different collections while maintaining the elevated aesthetic of the show.

Together, LUSH Hair and QM Beauty demonstrated the importance of beauty partnerships within fashion production—and how the right beauty collaborators can transform a collection from a clothing presentation into a fully realised visual experience.

Raising a Glass to Celebration

No Nigerian wedding celebration would be complete without a toast, and The Lagos Bridal Show brought that spirit to the event through its drinks partners.

Laurent-Perrier Champagne added a touch of French luxury to the occasion, creating an elevated champagne experience for guests and reinforcing the show’s positioning at the intersection of fashion, luxury and celebration.

Yellow Tail Wine brought a more relaxed and celebratory energy to the experience, giving guests an opportunity to enjoy the event while connecting with the brand in an environment built around weddings, relationships and celebration.

Both brands were supported by Ekulo Wine Group, the drinks partner behind the event’s beverage experience, helping to ensure that hospitality was an integral part of the overall show rather than an afterthought.

From the first cocktail to the final runway look, the beverage experience contributed to the atmosphere of sophistication and celebration that defined the evening.

More Than a Fashion Show

What made The Lagos Bridal Show particularly significant was its ambition to be more than a runway.

The show was conceived as a platform for the Nigerian bridal ecosystem—a space where designers could meet potential customers, brands could reach their target demographic, sponsors could create meaningful experiences, and couples could discover the people and products that could become part of their wedding journey.

For Nigerians in the diaspora and international couples looking to incorporate Nigerian fashion and culture into their celebrations, the show also presented an opportunity to discover the breadth of talent within the country’s fashion industry.

This is increasingly important as Nigerian weddings continue to attract international attention and Nigerian designers become part of celebrations far beyond the country’s borders.

Building the Future of Nigerian Bridal Fashion

The success of The Lagos Bridal Show ultimately points to something bigger than one event.

Nigeria has no shortage of extraordinary designers, beauty professionals, creative directors, stylists and wedding vendors. What has been missing is a consistent, dedicated platform capable of bringing these different parts of the industry together.

The Lagos Bridal Show is positioned to become that platform

With its combination of runway fashion, industry conversations, media engagement, brand activations and access to the bridal consumer, the show offers a new way of experiencing Nigerian bridal fashion—and a new opportunity for brands to participate in one of the country’s most vibrant consumer categories.

From the designers who brought their collections to life, to LUSH Hair and QM Beauty Cosmetics, who created the beauty looks, and Laurent-Perrier, Yellow Tail and Ekulo Wine Group, who elevated the celebration, the inaugural edition was made possible through a collective belief in the potential of Nigeria’s bridal industry.

And if the first edition is anything to go by, The Lagos Bridal Show is only getting started.

BellaNaija celebrated two decades at the Grand Red Carpet Experience under the High Fashion Icon theme. Nigerian men stepped out in vintage pinstripes, Victorian tailcoats, metallic jacquard, and royal regalia.

item.content:encoded:
Shawn Faqua, Larry Hector, and Yemi Cregx presenting three distinct menswear interpretations of the High Fashion Icon brief.

Pinstripes, Victorian tailoring, jacquard, coral beads and a very serious amount of headwear. The men at BellaNaija’s 20th anniversary Grand Red Carpet Experience clearly had their own ideas about what High Fashion Icon should look like, and they were not all heading in the same direction. Shawn Faqua went vintage, Larry Hector brought Victorian tailoring to the carpet, Yemi Cregx played with colour and proportion, while Sydney Ihonu looked to Eastern Nigerian royal regalia for his take on the theme.

The looks were part of a much bigger fashion story at the BellaNaija at 20 Grand Red Carpet Experience, where celebrities, creatives and industry figures came together to celebrate two decades of BellaNaija. With High Fashion Iconas the theme, the carpet became a place for guests to have fun with shape, tailoring, texture and personal style. While the ladies stepped out in everything from sculptural gowns to corseted suits and dramatic headpieces, the men brought their own interpretations to the brief.

Veekee James, Mercy Eke, and Prudent Gabriel attend the BellaNaija 20th Anniversary Grand Red Carpet Experience.

First up, Shawn Faqua went straight for old-school tailoring in a pinstriped three-piece suit. The wide crossover lapels gave the jacket a strong shape, while the structured button placement and broad trousers leaned into the proportions of classic menswear. He finished the look with a matching tie, dark sunglasses, a charcoal fedora and a walking cane, taking the vintage reference all the way through rather than stopping at the suit.

Shawn Faqua wearing a vintage-inspired pinstriped three-piece suit with wide crossover lapels for the High Fashion Icon theme.

Then there was Larry Hector, whose Victorian-inspired black tailcoat brought an entirely different mood to the carpet. The coat featured broad peak lapels and traditional button placement, worn with a white collar, black bow tie and black gloves. He added a tall black top hat to extend the silhouette upwards, while a crimson red feather boa fell across his shoulder, breaking up the black tailoring with a burst of colour and texture.

Larry Hector wearing a Victorian-inspired black tailcoat paired with a crimson feather boa for the High Fashion Icon theme.

Yemi Cregx took a softer route, working with blush, black and metallic tones. His iridescent blush jacquard blazer sat over a high-collared black shirt, complete with a structured neck wrap and pleated waist vest. He paired the top half with charcoal wide-leg flared trousers, rectangular sunglasses and a black leather handbag, creating a look built around contrast: soft colour against dark tailoring, fitted details against wider proportions.

Yemi Cregx interpreting the High Fashion Icon brief at the BellaNaija 20th anniversary celebration in a blush metallic jacquard blazer layered over a black high-collared shirt with a neck wrap, pleated vest, and wide-leg trousers.

Sydney Ihonu brought culture directly into his interpretation of High Fashion Icon, stepping onto the red carpet in an Eastern Nigerian royal ensemble. His look began with a deep burgundy undertunic beneath a golden-beige woven cape, cut with broad angular shoulders and finished with burgundy trim. From there, he layered on the details: a burgundy velvet cap topped with twin white feathers, red coral beads around his neck, matching wrist cuffs and a traditional hand-woven fur fan.

Sydney Ihonu wearing an Eastern Nigerian royal ensemble with coral beads and a feathered cap for BellaNaija at 20.

That mix of fashion and heritage gave Sydney’s look a very different place on the carpet. While the other men played with vintage tailoring, unusual proportions and rich fabrics, he used royal regalia as the foundation, bringing a distinctly Nigerian reference into the evening’s high-fashion conversation.

From Shawn Faqua’s pinstriped three-piece and Larry Hector’s top-hat-and-feather-boa combination to Yemi Cregx’s wide-leg proportions and Sydney Ihonu’s royal-inspired styling, the BellaNaija at 20 red carpet gave Nigerian menswear plenty of room to explore the High Fashion Icon brief in their own ways.

item.title: Uche Pedro’s High Fashion Icon Look for BellaNaija at 20 Was a Sculptural Crimson Gown
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Uche Pedro embraced BellaNaija at 20’s High Fashion Icon theme in a sculptural crimson gown with micro-pleating, an exaggerated shoulder and a ruffled trumpet skirt for the BellaNaija at 20 Grand Red Carpet Experience.

The post Uche Pedro’s High Fashion Icon Look for BellaNaija at 20 Was a Sculptural Crimson Gown appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Uche Pedro styled her crimson red gown with silver teardrop earrings, bronze eyeshadow, and a romantic high updo.

Uche Pedro, BellaNaija’s founder and CEO, clearly had High Fashion Icon in mind when she stepped onto the red carpet for BellaNaija’s 20th anniversary celebration. Her choice was a floor-length crimson red gown covered in sculptural micro-pleating, with an exaggerated shoulder, an asymmetrical neckline and a ruffled trumpet skirt that made the whole silhouette feel wonderfully larger than life.

And of course, there is a lot to look at.

The custom gown was built around a corseted waist, with diagonal, wave-like pleat lines running across the bodice to shape the figure before dropping into a trumpet skirt made from layers of circular ruffles. The effect was dramatic without needing a pile-on of accessories. The dress already had plenty going on, and Uche let its shape do the talking.

Uche Pedro wearing an architectural floor-length crimson red gown at the BellaNaija at 20 anniversary celebration.

That exaggerated shoulder detail was another thing that made the gown so interesting. The neckline sat off one shoulder, while the other side rose into a sculpted shape, creating an asymmetrical finish that gave the dress its fashion-forward edge. Then came the dropped waist and those layers of ruffles, which added volume from the hips down while keeping the upper half of the gown fitted.

Uche kept her accessories simple, pairing the crimson gown with silver teardrop earrings and a smooth silver cuff bracelet. The cooler silver against the rich red was a smart way to accessorise without competing with the dress. Her beauty look stayed in the same warm colour family, with bronze eyeshadow and a glossy lip, while her hair was pulled into a high updo finished with soft curtain bangs and braided coils arranged neatly at the crown.

Uche Pedro wearing a custom crimson red mermaid gown with sculptured micro-pleating for the High Fashion Icon theme.

The look was made for the occasion, too. BellaNaija turned 20 this year, and the Grand Red Carpet Experience brought together celebrities, creatives, fashion personalities and industry leaders to celebrate two decades of the platform. The theme, High Fashion Icon, gave guests plenty of room to interpret what the words meant to them, from sculptural gowns to statement tailoring and unexpected styling choices.

For Uche, the evening carried an extra layer of significance. item.content:encoded:
Wunmi Mosaku as Annie in Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, earning her first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Photo Credit: Wunmi Mosaku/Instagram

Wunmi Mosaku has officially had her Spirit Tunnel moment, and if you know anything about this hallway, you already know she was not going to simply walk through it.

The Oscar-nominated, BAFTA-winning actress brought plenty of personality to the backstage hallway of The Jennifer Hudson Show ahead of her appearance on the 6 October episode, where she joined Jennifer Hudson to talk about her upcoming film, The Social Reckoning.

Dressed in a light blue-teal halter-neck midi dress with a matching fabric belt and silver round buckle, Wunmi made her way towards the stage in metallic silver strappy heels. Her structured braids were neatly coiled at the crown, giving the look a polished finish as she stepped into the hallway and immediately got into the spirit of things.

And by “walked”, we mean Wunmi was dancing her way through.

She grooved down the carpet, swayed her hips, pointed, snapped her fingers and moved along to the music as the show’s production crew, writers and staff lined both sides of the corridor to cheer her on. And they had their own little song ready for her, singing:

In the zone, got Wunmi!
She’s a queen to us, you see!
Happy place is showing love…
Wunmi’s here, let’s turn her up!

Wunmi clearly enjoyed every second of it, beaming as she laughed with the crew, blew kisses, threw her hands up and pointed back at the people cheering her on. The tunnel quickly became a little celebration of its own, with everyone clapping, dancing and keeping the chant going as she made her way towards the stage.

She kept the fun going all the way to the stage doors, where the glowing “ON AIR” sign marked the end of the tunnel. Wunmi stepped through, struck a final pose, made a heart with her hands and waved to the audience before heading backstage.

It is easy to see why the Spirit Tunnel has become such a fun part of The Jennifer Hudson Show. The show’s staff use the tunnel to hype up guests with original chants and dance moves before they go on stage, turning that short walk from backstage into a proper celebration.

And Wunmi certainly gave them something to work with, matching their welcome with her own moves, smiles and plenty of personality. After that entrance, we are very curious to see what she and Jennifer got up to once the cameras were rolling.

item.content:encoded:
Minimie presents the final BBNaija Season 11 Week in Review, celebrating Top 3 finalists Aikou, Temi Nkem, and Sheba.

What a week! What a season! Just like that, the lights have gone out on the Big Brother Naija: Show Ya Sef house, and we are officially suffering from post-BBN withdrawal. After 10 whole weeks of unhinged chaos, epic wager displays, midnight kitchen politics, and endless gbas gbos, Season 11 has drawn its final curtain.

Through every single plot twist, emotional eviction, and late-night drama, Minimie ChinChin has been right there with us, delivering all the crunchy, delicious refreshment needed to fuel our watch parties while we rooted for our absolute favourite housemates. And as typical of our weekly date, you already know you have got to grab your favourite pack of Minimie ChinChin to snack on for this very last recap.

And darling, what a blockbuster week it was to wrap up the show.

From a second Head of House crown to a shocking disqualification that shook social media, and an emotional, historic Top 3 stage walk, the final stretch delivered everything we love about Biggie’s house. Settle in and crunch along—here is your ultimate breakdown of how the Show Ya Sef finale week went down.

A season that gave everything

Shoutout to all the housemates

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/pCgaz2MBkV

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

Barry’s Double HoH Triumph and The Final Campaign Hour

If there is one housemate who knows how to peak at the absolute right moment, it is Barry.

Closing out the season on a massive high, Barry went all out in a multi-stage, 15-minute obstacle course featuring familiar games from the season. Earning the highest overall score, he snatched his second Head of House title and made history as the final HoH of Season 11.

Biggie added a super sweet twist for the week, giving every single finalist a one-night stay in the iconic HoH Loft so everyone could enjoy the luxury before packing their bags. Barry chose Bluethopia as his Loft mate, while a high-stakes tiebreaker between Bluethopia, Flora, Oyin, and Ricky left Flora as the season’s final Benchwarmer.

Barry emerges as the final Head of House for Big Brother Naija Show Ya Sef Week 10.

When Nomination Hour rolled around, Biggie swapped the usual nerve-wracking voting for pure heart-to-heart pitches. Each finalist got two minutes in the diary room to campaign for why they deserved the ultimate crown—plus a twist. They were given one extra minute to campaign for a fellow finalist.

  • The Highlights: Keivo shared his dream of using the grand prize to become a pilot, before backing Aikou. Tram revealed he wants the win to launch his career as one of Nigeria’s biggest content streamers (and campaigned for Oyin). Meanwhile, Temi Nkem brought her signature theatrical flair—kneeling, rolling on the diary room floor, and pleading her case to Biggie before selflessly campaigning for Sheba.

The moment Big Brother announced Kievo’s removal and disqualification from BBNaija season 11 following his altercation with Tram last night.

What are your thoughts?

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/cIdBm2dUGk

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) September 29, 2026

Drama in the Final Stretch: Keivo’s Shock Disqualification

Just when everyone thought the housemates would cruise smoothly into Sunday night, Monday night brought a heartbreaking turn of events.

A heated disagreement over a shirt between Keivo and Tram spiraled out of control, resulting in physical violence. Following a mandatory gathering where Biggie played the footage for the entire house, Keivo was officially disqualified from Big Brother Naija Season 11.

Biggie reminded the remaining finalists that no level of frustration, communal living pressure, or personal grievance ever justifies physical violence. Keivo’s sudden exit brought his journey to an immediate end, leaving nine housemates in the final stretch for the ₦160 million prize package.

Keivo disqualified from Big Brother Naija Season 11 following a physical altercation.

The MIPOW Prize Pot Settled

It wasn’t all tears and tension, though. After weeks of fierce strategic battles, the Most Influential Player of the Week (MIPOW) race officially wrapped up.

Throughout the 10 weeks, every penalty, task win, and game-changing decision impacted the special prize pot. The final numbers locked in at a cool ₦10 million.

While the ultimate winner takes the ₦90 million main cash prize, this accumulated ₦10 million pot is being shared equally among the weekly MIPOW champs: Chimsom Chuka, Sultex, Abi, Sheba, Barry, Aikou, and Tram. Talk about a well-earned payout for playing the game so smartly.

What better way to open the grand finale than a grand performance from a grand artist?

@TeniEntertainer opening the #BBNaija finale

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/lJUMg4fUFT

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

Finale Night: The Evictions and A Historic Top 3 Walk

Sunday night was pure electric energy. Teni kicked off the festivities with a fire performance that had everyone on their feet, before Ebuka Obi -Uchendu took over to break hearts and fulfil dreams.

Ebuka Obi-Uchendu wearing high-waisted satin trousers and cutout dress shoes for the BBNaija finale.

One by one, the finalists took their bow:

  • Barry was the first to leave, wrapping up a stellar run as a two-time HoH, MIPOW winner, and Ultimate Veto Power holder.
  • Oyin departed shortly after in 8th place, followed by Ricky in 7th, who gave us endless charm and top-tier flirting all season.
  • Flora ended her incredible journey in 6th place (what a ride from being a Gambit to reinstatement), while Tram exited in 5th after a high-energy, headline-making run.
  • Bluethopia bowed out in 4th place, leaving the final race down to three incredible women: Aikou, Sheba, and Temi Nkem.

Bluethopia has been evicted!

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/2O6qeYJQBA

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

In a historic BBNaija first, Oshamo performed as Biggie asked the Top 3 to walk onto the stage together, breaking the traditional Top 2 format and making for an unforgettable visual moment.

The finalists, Sheba, Temi Nkem and Aikou have a left the house.

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/sa3CSOLdoZ

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

All Hail the Queen: Temi Nkem Takes the Crown

When the moment finally came, Ebuka held his breath, the crowd roared, and Temi Nkem was officially named the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11: Show Ya Sef.

At just 21 years old, the London-born Accounting and Finance student walked away with the grand ₦160 million prize package—including ₦90 million cold cash and a shiny new SUV.

The moment Temi Nkem was announced the winner of the #BBNaija season 11.

#BBNaijaS11 #BNxBBNaija11 #BBNaija https://t.co/btjxUN9AAe

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

Looking back at her journey, it is easy to see why the public fell in love with her:

  • Unapologetically Herself: Right from Day 1 when housemates complained about her UK accent during the wager brief, Temi Nkem refused to shrink herself to fit in.
  • Zero Immunity, Pure Grit: Remarkably, Temi Nkem survived week after week without ever holding individual immunity or a MIPOW save until Barry’s Ultimate Veto save in the semi-finals. She faced the public vote repeatedly and survived every single time.
  • Unmatched Content and Personality: Whether she was running a chaotic BB Bucks heist, locking down her “house family” (with Araga and Goddessa as her parents and Sheba as Aunt Shibi), or obsessively making endless batches of custard for house reviews, she was impossible to ignore.

Temi Nkem receiving her ₦90 million cash prize cheque from Ebuka Obi-Uchendu at the Big Brother Naija Season 11 grand finale.

Temi Nkem now officially enters the history books as the fifth female winner of Big Brother Naija, joining Mercy Eke, Phyna, Ilebaye, and Imisi.

She came, she served top-tier entertainment, she stood her ground, and she conquered. Gbam! Gbammer! Gbammest!

Big Brother Naija Season 11: Show Ya Sef may have officially come to an end, but you know what hasn’t? The deliciously crunch-tastic, satisfying refreshment of Minimie ChinChin. item.content:encoded:
If you run a small business in Nigeria, you probably know how this goes.

Someone wants time off, they send you a WhatsApp message. You say yes, life moves on, and two weeks later there is a scheduling conflict nobody saw coming. A new person joins the team and their details go into a spreadsheet that half the office has access to and nobody updates. Payday arrives and something is off and you are not entirely sure why.

For a while, it works. Then the team grows, and suddenly it really does not.

This is the reality Adetoun Adele-Muraina and Adetola Abolarinwa watched play out across business after business through their HR consulting firm, Bridgemead Consulting. Working closely with Nigerian founders and business leaders, they saw the same pattern repeat itself: companies that had outgrown their informal systems but could not find a solution that actually fit where they were.

The tools that existed were either built for large corporations with dedicated HR departments, or designed for markets with very different realities. For the millions of small and growing businesses that sit at the heart of Nigeria’s economy, there was a gap.
So they built something to fill it.

PeoplePulse Africa is an HR platform built specifically for African MSMEs. Payroll, leave management, performance reviews, employee records and compliance, all in one place, designed to be simple enough to use without an HR department and powerful enough to actually run your people operations as the business grows.

“We kept seeing the same challenges across different businesses,” says Adetoun. “It was never a lack of care. Founders wanted to do right by their people. The right tools just were not there for them.”

The platform launched into paid pilot earlier this year and has been onboarding businesses since. PeoplePulse Africa has participated in programmes within the wider business and technology ecosystem, including the Providus Bank SME Programme and the Village Capital x Standard Chartered Women in Tech Accelerator 2026. PeoplePulse is also currently participating in a founder programme by Antler Africa, a venture capital firm.

“We are building something we genuinely believe in,” says Adetola. “The businesses we built this for deserve better than what existed before.“

With 39 million MSMEs in Nigeria and only one in ten currently automating their HR processes, the opportunity is significant. More importantly, so is the need.

Businesses can request a demo or join the early access waitlist at peoplepulseafrica.com

About PeoplePulse Africa

PeoplePulse Africa is an HR platform built for African small and medium-sized businesses. Founded by Adetoun Adele-Muraina and Adetola Abolarinwa, it covers payroll, leave, performance management, and compliance in one simple platform.

item.content:encoded:
Agbara Nla: The Return brings spiritual warfare and high-stakes family drama to cinema screens nationwide this October. Photo Credit: Damilola Mike-Bamiloye/Instagram 

There is plenty to choose from at the Nigerian box office this month, with October’s Nollywood cinema slate moving between spiritual battles, gritty thrillers, Lagos comedy and a sweeping historical drama.

Familiar names are taking on roles both in front of and behind the camera, bringing very different stories to the big screen. Whether you prefer a story rooted in faith, a film that keeps you guessing or a good dose of Nigerian humour, these five films offer very different reasons to make a trip to the cinema this month.

Here are five Nollywood movies showing in Nigerian cinemas this October.

Agbara Nla: The Return

Fans of Mount Zion Film Ministries will recognise the name Agbara Nla, but Agbara Nla: The Return gives the 1993 classic a new theatrical treatment for a contemporary audience. Following its preview run, the film revisits the spiritual battle at the heart of the original while exploring legacy, redemption and the unseen forces affecting families in modern Nigeria.

Mike Bamiloye stars as Isawuru in Agbara Nla: The Return, a faith-based drama exploring spiritual battles and legacy. Photo Credit: Agbara Nla/Instagram 

Mike Bamiloye, Damilola Mike–Bamiloye, Joshua Bamiloye and Aanu Kolade lead the cast, with Mike Bamiloye credited as writer. Damilola Mike–Bamiloye and Joshua “JayMikee” Bamiloye direct, while Mount Zion Film Ministries serves as producer.

Black Market

Black Market takes audiences into the dangerous side of urban survival, where underground networks, economic pressure and difficult choices collide. The gritty thriller stars Lateef Adedimeji, Linda Ejiofor– Suleiman, Ibrahim Yekini (Itele), Taye Arimoro, Omowunmi Dada, Teniola Aladese, Scarlet Gomez, Andrew Bunting and Susan Pwajok, with Abdul Tijani–Ahmed and Fatimah Binta Gimsay credited as writers.

Gimsay also directs the film, while Nora Awolowo produces. Before its nationwide cinema release, Black Market made headlines after its screening at Tafawa Balewa Square, where the production set a Guinness World Record for the largest film screening attendance in a single location.

Star Lomo

For something lighter, Star Lomo brings Kamo State’s street comedy to the big screen. The comedy-drama follows an ambitious local personality navigating neighbourhood rivalries, unexpected challenges and the funny complications that come with trying to make a name for himself. Akinyoola “Kamo State” Ayoola stars alongside Ibrahim Chatta, Abiola Adebayo, Lateef Adedimeji, Kayode Jnr. Ojuolape and Peller. Kamo State also wrote the film and produced it under Kamo State Productions, while Kayode Kasum directs.

No Fury

Coming to cinemas on 23 October, No Fury leans into psychological suspense, betrayal and revenge. The story centres on a seemingly happy couple whose life begins to unravel after a hidden betrayal comes to light, setting off a chain of events that pushes their relationships and loyalties to the limit. Jim Iyke, Nse Ikpe-Etim, Lilian Esoro, Tina Mba, Jide Awobona, Nosa Rex and Prisca Okeke star in the film. Akay Mason and his team are credited as writers, Mason directs, and Akay Mason Productions produces.

Jim Iyke and Nse Ikpe-Etim star in No Fury, a gripping thriller about love, hidden betrayal, and revenge. Photo Credit: FilmOne/Instagram

King Kosoko: The Battle for Lagos

King Kosoko: The Battle for Lagos takes audiences back to 19th-century Lagos for a historical story centred on Oba Kosoko and his fight to protect his sovereignty amid external pressure and internal political rivalries. Femi Adebayo plays Oba Kosoko, with Odunlade Adekola as Oba Akintoye, alongside Jide Kosoko, Gabriel Afolayan, Femi Branch and Tina Mba. Adebayo Tijani and his team wrote the film, Tijani directs, and the production is backed by Ayo Ajayi, Segun Olojo–Kosoko and Teqsus Studios.

Set between the Odu community and Lagos, The Four follows Esosa and three fiercely loyal women through a fight that tests their courage, faith and friendship. Motherhood and the strength of women are at the heart of their journey, giving the film’s message, ‘no one fights alone,’ a deeply personal meaning.

item.content:encoded:
Forty-two young women from the 19th edition of the She Creates residential camp recently stepped out of the classroom and into the future. Aligning perfectly with the camp’s focus on AI, Future Skills, and Digital Readiness, W.TEC took the cohort on an eye-opening excursion to the brand new Science Experience Centre (SEC) at the Lagos State Ministry of Innovation, Science, and Technology, Alausa, Lagos.

The Lagos Science Experience Centre is one of its kind in Nigeria, a pioneering initiative established by a state government to make science, technology and innovation more interactive, accessible and exciting for young people. Our campers were privileged to be among the first sets of visitors to experience this remarkable and inspiring facility.

About She Creates Summer Camp

The She Creates Summer Camp for girls is a flagship programme of W.TEC, a transformative summer learning (residential-camp) programme designed to inspire, educate, and empower secondary school girls with world class Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) skills. Since its launch in 2008, the camp has become a living institution , a place where numerous girls discover their potential, build lifelong confidence, and grow into tech driven innovators.

Over the years, the camp has been hosted across multiple Nigerian states, including Lagos, Kwara Anambra, reaching girls from both urban and underserved communities. Today, the She Creates Camp proudly records over 700 girls trained in its residential and non-residential editions, with alumnae excelling in university, careers, entrepreneurship, and community leadership.

From the moment our 2026 Lagos camp participants arrived, the centre transformed learning from something they encountered mainly in textbooks and classrooms into an exciting, hands-on experience. The girls enthusiastically explored:

  • Virtual Reality (VR)
  • 3D Printing
  • Drone Technology
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Video Game Design
  • Digital Drawing
  • Interactive Chemistry
  • Biology
  • First Aid

The immersive environment struck a perfect balance between learning, discovery and play. Complex concepts were brought to life through interactive demonstrations and practical experiences, helping the girls see science and technology from an entirely new perspective.

Changing How Girls See STEM

The experience was particularly powerful because it challenged some of the girls’ previous perceptions of traditionally difficult subjects such as Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics. What can sometimes feel abstract or intimidating in the classroom became exciting and understandable when experienced through technology and practical demonstrations.

In their feedback, the girls expressed how much they loved the entire experience and how the excursion had changed the way they viewed these subjects. They were especially enthusiastic about the centre’s interactive experiences, with Virtual Reality emerging as the girls’ favourite, followed by the Drone Technology and Video Game sections.

For many of the campers, the visit was more than an excursion, it was a mind changing experience that demonstrated that STEM can be creative, exciting, practical and fun.

The magic of the SEC wasn’t reserved for the students alone. The adult camp chaperones were equally captivated, letting their inner kids out as they eagerly rolled up their sleeves and joined the interactive sessions alongside the girls.

As W.TEC continues its mission of encouraging more girls to explore and pursue STEM, experiences like this are invaluable. They help girls move beyond simply learning about science and technology to experiencing what is possible when knowledge, creativity and innovation come together.

We commend the Lagos State Ministry of Innovation, Science, and Technology for creating this phenomenal space for discovery and inspiration. The Science Experience Centre is a powerful example of how experiential learning can ignite curiosity, reshape perceptions and inspire the next generation of innovators.

For our She Creates campers, their visit was a memorable step into the future and a reminder that the subjects they once considered difficult can also become the ones they love.

Remember that Lagos recreation of Chanel’s Métiers d’Art collection that took over social media? Well, Rachael Ojuromi has taken that story all the way to Paris.

The 22-year-old Nigerian model and creative director has officially walked in Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2027 show at the Grand Palais in Paris. It is a full-circle fashion story that began with Rachael and her close friend and stylist, Debby Fasingha, recreating Chanel looks with thrifted pieces around Lagos, including on the Red Line rail overpass in Yaba.

The recreation caught the attention of Chanel creative director Matthieu Blazy, who commented “Everything” under their viral video on Instagram. That moment helped put Rachael’s creative work in front of a much wider fashion audience, and her modelling career soon picked up pace, with agency representation now spanning New York, Paris and London.

Rachael Ojuromi recreating a Chanel Métiers d’Art tailored look using second-hand clothing sourced in Lagos. Photo Credit: Rachael Ojuromi/Instagram

Before Chanel, Rachael had already been building a creative career of her own. She is the founder of The Process Africa, a platform focused on emerging African talent, and her background in film, writing and communication has shaped the way she approaches fashion. Rather than treating clothes as the whole story, her work often brings together styling, location and visual storytelling, which was clear in the Lagos Chanel recreation that first caught international attention.

For Rachael and Debby, the idea was simple but ambitious: recreate Chanel’s Métiers d’Art looks using second-hand pieces sourced around Lagos, then reinterpret the luxury house’s runway imagery through their own creative lens. The result travelled far beyond the original setting, eventually leading Rachael from Lagos street scenes to one of Chanel’s biggest global stages.

Rachael Ojuromi styling a thrifted floral dress in Lagos next to the Chanel runway reference. Photo Credit: Rachael Ojuromi/Instagram

Rachael has always connected with Matthieu Blazy’s work, praise she shared when reflecting on his Chanel direction: “I connect with what he does so much because of the cunning simplicity in the presentation of his ideas, such grand stories presented in completely digestible ways.” That same philosophy shaped her own work with Debby Fasingha, taking their Lagos recreations all the way from social media feeds to the Grand Palais.

On 6 October 2026, Rachael walked in Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2027 presentation at the Grand Palais. The show, titled La Conversation — Part Three — Different Faces of the Same Coin, placed her among the models presenting Matthieu Blazy’s latest collection for the French fashion house.

Rachael Ojuromi making her Chanel runway debut at the Grand Palais in Paris.

And that makes the journey from those thrifted Chanel recreations in Lagos to the actual Chanel runway in Paris all the more striking. What started as a creative reinterpretation with a friend has opened a new chapter in Rachael Ojuromi’s modelling career, with Paris now firmly part of her story.

item.content:encoded:
In January 2012, Wawira Njiru raised A$1,680 to start Food4Education. As someone who grew up seeing children in her community struggle with hunger, and after speaking with local schools, she realised that for many children, food was inseparable from education. It was what made education possible.

Fourteen years later, Food4Education has grown into an organisation serving 700,000 children every school day and working towards reaching one million by July 2027. Along the way, Njiru has built more than a school-feeding programme. Food4Education has become a model for how investing in children can strengthen local agriculture, create jobs, build infrastructure and contribute to Africa’s wider human capital.

The scale of that work has earned Njiru global recognition. In 2026, she was named a DVF Leadership Award honouree, joining a group of women recognised for their leadership and impact. She was also named to the TIME100 Next list, which celebrates emerging leaders shaping the future. Yet, for Njiru, the recognition is less about her than it is about what the work represents: an African organisation, built by Africans to solve an African challenge, proving what is possible when local ideas are given the opportunity to grow.

In this conversation, Wawira Njiru reflects on the journey from feeding 25 children with a basic kitchen to building a system serving hundreds of thousands, her vision for an Africa where no child has to learn hungry, the importance of African ownership in solving African problems, and what it takes to build something that can outlive its founder.

Wawira Njiru

Hello Wawira. Congratulations on being named a 2026 DVF Leadership Award honouree and, most recently, to the TIME100 Next list. At this stage of your journey, what does this recognition mean to you and the work that you do?

It means a great deal, particularly because of what the DVF Leadership Awards represent: women who have dared to build, lead and create change in their own way. But I think recognition has changed for me over the years. When I started Food4Education, I was 21 years old, feeding 25 children from one small kitchen in Ruiru. My biggest ambition was to reach 100 children. Today, we serve 700,000 children every school day, and we are working toward one million by July 2027.

So when recognition happens, I think less about myself and more about what it says about the work. It says that an African organisation, built by Africans to solve an African challenge, can build something at enormous scale and that the world is paying attention.

I also think about the thousands of people who built this with us. The women working in our kitchens, the farmers who grow our food, the parents who contribute to their children’s meals, our team, our government partners and, of course, the children themselves. This recognition belongs to that entire ecosystem.

I said at the DVF Awards that what began as a passion project has become the beginning of my life’s work. That is really how I feel. The recognition is wonderful, but what excites me most is how much further there is to go.

You started with 25 children to solve child hunger and education. Today, you are thinking about millions of children and a model that could influence how Africa approaches school feeding. If there were no limitations, what would your absolute dream for Food4Education be?

My dream is actually very simple: that no African child ever has to learn hungry. But achieving that requires us to think much bigger than food.

By 2050, one in four people on Earth will be African. That makes investing in the continent’s next generation one of the greatest opportunities in the world. The question is whether we invest in those children now. Africa’s greatest asset is its human capital, and we cannot wait until children become adults to begin investing in them.

I like that

Thank you. So if there were no constraints, I would want every African government to have the infrastructure, financing, technology and local supply chains required to feed every child in school, every day. I would want those systems to create markets for African farmers, jobs for young people and women, stronger local food systems and healthier, better-educated children.

We are beginning to see what that can look like in Kenya. Food4Education now serves 700,000 meals every school day. More than 80 per cent of our produce is sourced locally; we have created more than 6,000 jobs, and our procurement has already created a market worth more than $50 million for Kenyan farmers.

These are really impressive numbers, but what would you love people to say about the work in, let’s put a number, 30 years from now?

Thirty years from now, I hope people don’t talk about Food4Education primarily as an organisation that fed a lot of children. I hope they say we helped change what Africa believed was possible. That we showed school feeding could be public infrastructure. That investing in children could strengthen an entire economy. And that we built something strong enough to continue without me.

That, to me, would be success.

I like your ideas around African ownership. How do you think Africa can stop importing solutions to problems that Africans are capable of solving themselves?

I don’t think Africa’s problem is a shortage of ideas or talent. We have extraordinary builders across this continent. What we need is the confidence, capital and institutions to back them at the scale of the problems they are trying to solve.

There is also a tendency to think that something built elsewhere can simply be imported and replicated. But context matters enormously. When we enter a new country, our job is not to arrive with a Kenyan template and say, “Here is the answer.” You have to understand what already exists. What is government already doing? What infrastructure is already there? What are families already contributing? What do farmers already grow? Where are the gaps?

What would you want African governments, philanthropists and young Africans to understand about building solutions that are genuinely rooted in the continent?

One of our principles is to meet governments and communities where they are, not where we wish they were. Scale comes from building on what already exists and strengthening it.

And this is why I believe African governments have to be central. Philanthropy can take risks, help prove what works and provide catalytic capital, but you cannot philanthropically fund public infrastructure forever. In Kenya, families and government are investing alongside us. That shared ownership is part of what makes the system sustainable. Through FY27, government and family co-investment alongside Food4Education will total nearly $70 million.

For young Africans, I would say: don’t wait for perfect conditions. Food4Education started with about $1,200, 25 children and one very basic kitchen. I have always asked, “What is accessible to me? What can I do with what is around me?”

Start there. Prove something. Learn. Build trust. Then keep pushing it to the next level.

At what point did you realise that Food4Education could not just be about giving children a meal, but about changing the systems around food, education, employment and opportunity?

I don’t think there was one dramatic moment. The system revealed itself as we grew. At the beginning, the problem looked very immediate: a child is hungry, so feed the child. But even that first meal required a cook, food, a kitchen, a school willing to work with us and money to pay for the next meal. As we grew, every part of that became a system.

If you are feeding hundreds of thousands of children, you need farmers producing food at scale. You need kitchens and logistics. You need technology that tells you how many children ate and where. You need financing. You need government. You need thousands of people doing their jobs well every single day.

And then you realise that all of those things create value themselves. A school meal creates demand for a farmer. It creates a job for a worker. It requires infrastructure. It strengthens local supply chains. And ultimately, it is an investment in the human capital of a child.

What have you learned about building something that can outlive its founder?

Building something that outlives you means accepting that eventually it cannot depend on your energy, relationships or ability to solve every problem. It has to become institutional. The economics have to work. The data has to be visible. Government and communities need a stake in it. You need leaders who can make decisions without you.

I want Food4Education to become the kind of institution where the mission remains absolutely clear even when I am no longer in the room.

item.title: From London to Biggie’s House: 5 Things to Know About BBNaija Season 11 Winner Temi Nkem
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com

21-year-old content creator Temi Nkem won Big Brother Naija Season 11 with 25.87% of the final vote, claiming the ₦160m grand prize across her 70-day journey in Biggie's house.

The post From London to Biggie’s House: 5 Things to Know About BBNaija Season 11 Winner Temi Nkem appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
BBNaija housemate Temi Nkem celebrating her Nigerian heritage in custom white lace and traditional coral bead accessories. Photo Credit: Temi Nkem/Instagram

And just like that, we have a new Big Brother Naija winner! On Sunday night, 4th October 2026, 21-year-old content creator Temi Nkem was crowned the winner of the Show Ya Sef edition after 70 days in Biggie’s house.

Temi secured 25.87% of the final vote, edging ahead of first runner-up Aikou, who finished with 23.68%. Along with the title came a ₦160 million grand prize package, including ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and additional sponsored prizes.

Now that we have watched her go from housemate to BBNaija champion, it is time to get to know the woman behind the name. From her life in London and Lagos to her studies, content creation career and those 70 days in Biggie’s house, here are five things to know about Temi Nkem.

Temi Nkem, Accounting and Finance student and digital content creator who won Big Brother Naija Season 11. Photo Credit: Temi Nkem/Instagram

Her Real Name, Age and London-to-Lagos Background

First things first, who is Temi Nkem? Her full name is Temitope Chigbue, and at 21, she is officially the newest winner of Big Brother Naija.

Temi was born and raised in London, England, but she has always had strong ties to Nigeria. Her father is from Ibusa in Delta State, while her mother is from Ebute Metta, Lagos. She relocated to Lagos before joining BBNaija, so the Season 11 house was not her first introduction to life in Nigeria.

She Is an Accounting and Finance Student Who Also Creates Content

Reality TV may be her biggest headline right now, but there is more to Temi than her time on the show. She is an Accounting and Finance university student with an interest in treasury studies.

And when she is not studying, she is creating content. Temi works as a lifestyle content creator and digital influencer, sharing fashion content, daily vlogs and personal commentary with her online community.

Temi Nkem styled in a black asymmetric evening dress with heavy beadwork, corset bodice, and auburn-tinted hair. Photo Credit: Temi Nkem/Instagram

Her BBNaija Season 11 Journey Came With Plenty of Twists

Temi’s 70 days in the house certainly gave viewers plenty to follow. She entered the competition as one of 24 housemates and eventually made it all the way to the final nine.

One of the biggest twists in her journey came during the September fake eviction, when she was removed from the main house before returning directly to the competition. She also had to navigate the changing house dynamics during the BB Bucks era, form alliances and find her footing as the weeks went by.

Her outspoken personality also made her a regular part of the conversations around the show, and by finale night, she had secured her place among the final contenders for the crown.

She Is the Fifth Female Winner of Big Brother Naija

Temi’s win has also added her name to an important part of Big Brother Naija history. She is now the fifth female housemate to win the show, following Mercy Eke, Phyna, Ilebaye and Imisi.

And then there is the prize. Temi is leaving the house with a ₦160 million package, made up of ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and additional prizes from the season’s sponsors.

Temi Nkem receiving her ₦90 million cash prize cheque from Ebuka Obi-Uchendu at the Big Brother Naija Season 11 grand finale. Photo Credit: Temi Nkem/Instagram

What Does Temi Want to Do After BBNaija?

So, what comes next for the new BBNaija winner? Temi already has her sights set on growing her career in digital media.

She enjoys golfing, walking and checking out local food spots, and she plans to launch a lifestyle video blog after the show. She is also interested in working with global fashion and entertainment brands, giving her a chance to take the content creator side of her career even further.

item.content:encoded:
Directors Arie and Chuko Esiri with cast members Sophie Okonedo, David Oyelowo, India Amarteifio, and Toheeb Jimoh at the Cannes Film Festival. Photo Credit: Fortune Nwafor/Instagram

It is never too early to start planning your December watchlist, and if you are already mapping out the films worth making time for, Clarissa deserves a prime spot on your radar.

Directed by Nigerian twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri, following their critically acclaimed debut Eyimofe (This Is My Desire), the film reimagines Virginia Woolf’s classic 1925 novel Mrs. Dalloway, shifting its story from post-war London to the lively backdrop of modern Lagos. The narrative follows Clarissa, played by Oscar nominee Sophie Okonedo, as she prepares to host a high-society party at her home. As the hours unfold, long-buried memories, past loves, and unresolved emotions begin to resurface.

Ayo Edebiri, David Oyelowo, India Amarteifio, and Toheeb Jimoh in Lagos during production for Clarissa. Photo Credit: India Amarteifio/Instagram

Running parallel to Clarissa’s journey is Septimus, played by Fortune Nwafor, a young soldier dealing with the hidden trauma of his past. The film moves seamlessly between their worlds, contrasting the glamour of Lagos high society with the quiet, internal struggles of those often overlooked by the world around them.

The ensemble cast brings together a remarkable mix of Nigerian and international stars. India Amarteifio plays young Clarissa, while David Oyelowo stars alongside Toheeb Jimoh, who portrays his younger self. Nikki Amuka–Bird and Ayo Edebiri also star, alongside Jude Akuwudike, Danny Sapani, Modesinuola Ogundiwin, Chuks Joseph, and Nollywood icon Joke Silva.

Cast members of Clarissa attending an evening event at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2026. Photo Credit: India Amarteifio/Instagram

Written by Chuko Esiri and produced by Theresa Park, Nicholas Weinstock, Arie Esiri, and Chuko Esiri, Clarissa premiered at the Cannes Film Festival’s Directors’ Fortnight before being acquired by NEON. The film is scheduled to open in select cinemas on 11th December 2026.

Akin Faminu has another big fashion milestone to celebrate, and this one takes him all the way to Paris. The Nigerian medical doctor, fashion creative, and content creator has been inducted into The Business of Fashion 500 Class of 2026, joining 500 of the figures shaping the global fashion industry.

item.content:encoded:
Sculpted hourglass tailoring, high-neck turtleneck layer, and oversized hat worn by Veekee James at the BellaNaija at 20 Grand Red Carpet Experience.

How do you celebrate impact? How do you measure the extent of the impact you have had on people, industries and culture over two decades? How does BellaNaija show Nigeria and the world just how much it has contributed to fashion, entertainment, media, business and culture?

Perhaps the best way is to bring the people who have been part of that story into one room. On the 2nd of October, BellaNaija brought personalities together for a Grand Red Carpet Experience, as a remarkable way to celebrate 20 years of BellaNaija. We marked our 20th anniversary with a grand celebration themed “High Fashion Icon,” bringing together personalities from different parts of Nigeria’s creative and business landscape. It was a glamorous red carpet event, yes, but it was also significant.

For two decades, BellaNaija has documented the people, moments and movements shaping African culture. It has covered weddings, fashion, entertainment, business, lifestyle and personal stories. BellaNaija transcended from being a cultural archive to a culture shaper; from a culture observer to the culture. The work grew so much that it needed to be properly compartmentalised. BellaNaija Editorial continues supporting African creatives; BellaNaija Weddings expanded as a home for African love stories, and BellaNaija Style and Beauty became the home of African fashion, style and everything glam.

For its 20th anniversary, it made sense to celebrate not only the platform, but the people and industries that have grown alongside it. These are people whose careers, work and influence exist within the same cultural ecosystem BellaNaija has spent 20 years documenting. Bringing them together was almost like bringing different chapters of Nigeria’s modern cultural story into one room.

That is why the Grand Red Carpet Experience felt bigger than an anniversary party. It was a reflection of what BellaNaija has become; the star power that commands the influence to bring culture shapers together.

Social media had not yet transformed how people consumed culture, African entertainment had not reached today’s level of global visibility, and digital media in Nigeria was still finding its feet. Two decades later, BellaNaija has remained part of the conversation, documenting the changes and, in many ways, helping shape them.

So, how do you celebrate 20 years of that? Bring the people you have impacted, and the people who have helped you make an impact, together. You gather the people. You create a room where fashion designers can meet entertainers, media personalities can meet entrepreneurs, and cultural figures can celebrate alongside the people whose work they have helped document.

You put them on a red carpet. You give them a theme. And you let the pictures and memories tell the story. The success of the BellaNaija Grand Red Carpet Experience, therefore, was not only in how beautiful the night looked. It was in what the gathering represented. Twenty years is a long time for any media platform. But BellaNaija did not simply mark the number. It used the occasion to look at the people, stories and industries that have made the journey meaningful.

item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, the 4th of October, 2026, Big Brother Naija Season 11 came to an end. Despite all that was said about the season, it remained unpredictable till the end. No one could say for certain there was a clear winner. The theme of the year is “Show Ya Sef”, and almost every housemate showed themselves. Even when the final three, AIkou, Temi Nkem and Sheba, went on stage, no one could pick out a clear winner from the three. Until Ebuka Obi-Uchendu announced the winner, everyone was glued to the screen, wondering who he’d mention, who’d be the winner of a season that has given us many things.

Now that the season is over and the winner is known, let’s look at some of the major highlights of the season that made it a remarkable and unforgettable one:

Temi Nkem, the Winner

No matter the matter, the biggest highlight of the season will be the winner. No matter how much drama, ships and controversies the season gave, what matters is knowing the winner, because that is all everyone in the house went to compete for. Yesterday, Temi Nkem was announced as the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11, winning a total prize of 160 million naira. 90 million naira cash prize, and other prizes spread across gifts.

Temi Nkem has always been clear that she’s gunning to win the season since the day she entered the house. While others could be seen doing more, Temi Nkem seemed like the daughter of the house, but she was giving subtle drama and forming alliances. Eventually, she was crowned the winner.

Temi Nkem is officially crowned the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11.

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) October 4, 2026

Neche’s Voluntary Exit

Early in the season, Neche took an early voluntary exit to leave the house. While it is still mostly unknown why she left the house, it was the first emotional rollercoaster that happened in the house. Housemates were shocked when she announced she was leaving, and some almost didn’t believe it. Despite winning the Head of House once, she left early in the season, and her exit remains one of the highlights of the season.

: Neche has exited #BBNaija Season 11 due to personal reasons.

Neche had an incredible journey in the house, winning several tasks and becoming a Head of House.

Thank you for your time in the house, Neche. BellaNaija wishes you all the very best.

— BellaNaija (@bellanaija) August 17, 2026

Keivo and Nomy’s Disqualifications

Keivo and Nomy were removed from the house for different reasons. Nomy was disqualified for constantly disobeying Biggie’s rules; she repeatedly refused to wear her bench warmer vest and did not respond to Biggie in a timely manner. In contrast, Keivo was disqualified for getting into a fight with Tram. The argument between them escalated, and Keivo struck Tram multiple times. As a result, he was immediately called to the storeroom and removed from the house.

Aikou finished as the 1st runner-up of the season, but he is one of the most talked-about of the season. Apart from being one of the Gambits, the way he spoke and carried himself in the house was on people’s lips. Anytime Ebuka Obi-Uchendu asked him a question, he would take his time to respond, which fascinated many of his fans.

Good bye, Kievo. You had your time in the house.

The Gamibits Twist

For 5 weeks, Flora and Aikou were the Gambits in the house. For the first time, the Gambits were introduced as housemates who were only there as spectators. item.content:encoded:
Veekee James, Mercy Eke, and Prudent Gabriel attend the BellaNaija 20th Anniversary Grand Red Carpet Experience.

The theme was High Fashion Icon, and the ladies clearly got the memo! BellaNaija turned 20, and for the Grand Red Carpet Experience, the red carpet became the place to see just how far our favourite style stars could take the brief.

After two decades of chronicling African lifestyle, culture and entertainment, BellaNaija celebrated the milestone with a night that called for fashion with a little more imagination. And the ladies showed up ready for it, stepping out in sculptural gowns, sharp tailoring, statement coats, dramatic headpieces and plenty of details that demanded a second look.

Mercy Eke wearing an Amy Aghomi coat-gown with cobalt blue pointed-toe slingback heels for BellaNaija at 20.

Veekee James went straight for the big fashion moment in a custom oxblood leather coat-gown, complete with a high-neck turtle detail, exaggerated hips and an ultra-wide-brim hat. Mercy Eke took a cooler route in ice-blue velvet with cobalt accents and pearl swirl details, while Prudent Gabriel gave us power dressing with an off-white corseted suit, asymmetric sheer tulle pleating and a dramatic pleated halo headpiece.

Veekee James in custom oxblood leather coat gown with exaggerated hips and saucer hat at BellaNaija 20th Anniversary Grand Red Carpet Experience.

Then came Mide Iwasokun in a sculptural white gown with a dramatic cascading train, while Osas Ighodaro brought metallic glamour to the carpet in an architectural ivory and gold creation.

And that was only part of the fashion conversation. From the silhouettes to the headpieces, textures and unexpected styling choices, the ladies had plenty of fun with the High Fashion Icon brief, giving BellaNaija’s 20th celebration a red carpet filled with looks worth pausing for.

Osas Ighodaro wearing architectural ivory and gold corseted ballgown with pleated fan structure at BellaNaija 20th Anniversary Grand Red Carpet Experience.

Two decades of BellaNaija deserved a fashion moment to match, and the ladies certainly understood the assignment.
